KANJIDON / NOTES FROM JAPAN

Suica says goodbye to its penguin.
DoDon has already
sent his CV.

Three candidates, a controversial farewell and a deep-sea fish convinced his moment has finally arrived. But first: why was there a penguin on a travel card?

Kanjidon Team · 23 September 2026

Some things instantly bring Japan to mind: convenience store chimes, punctual trains, that penguin on your Suica watching as you discover your balance is 37 yen.

Well. The penguin is packing his bags. And no, he isn’t just changing lines.

JR East has begun choosing the next mascot for its transport and payment card. There are three candidates. The internet has convened the court of design. DoDon has opened Canva to tidy up his CV.

HOLD ON AT THE GATE

The penguin is still here.

His departure is scheduled for the end of fiscal year 2026, meaning March 2027. The three designs aren’t a newly hired trio: they are alternatives for a single successor. JR East’s timeline ↗

01 / A NAME THAT FLOWS

Why is it called Suica?
No, it didn’t start in the fruit aisle.

Suica stands for Super Urban Intelligent CArd. A very serious English name for a card we often use to buy an onigiri and catch a train. It also echoes スイスイ, sui sui: moving smoothly, without a hitch. [1]

The little language bonus? Suika, すいか, also means “watermelon” in Japanese. Same sound, different plans: you top up one and slice up the other.

スイスイ
sui sui

“Smoothly, with ease.”
The ticket gate, yes. Finding the right exit at Shinjuku? Let’s see.

02 / THE COLLEAGUE EVERYONE LIKED

So what was the penguin doing there?

More than you might think. The character comes from Chiharu Sakazaki’s picture books and was chosen for Suica’s launch in 2001. The penguin suited the “sui sui” movement the card promised: gliding through the gates. [2]

Originally intended for a campaign, he became the face of the service, made it onto the card and did what good mascots do: turned a useful object into something people love. The creators tell the story in this interview.

It’s no longer “my contactless payment device”. It’s “my penguin card”. A very different relationship.

03 / THE REBRANDING MEETING

Why is JR East changing mascots?

The official reason is tied to Suica Renaissance: JR East’s plan to expand Suica beyond transport and small payments into more areas of daily life. A new chapter for the service, a new character alongside it. The change was announced on 11 November 2025. [3]

In corporate language, the penguin is “graduating”. Twenty-five years of ticket gates and they give you a bouquet. He smiles for the photo. We’re already at “fine, but who’s going to look after him?”

The announcement concerns his role as mascot. It doesn’t mean Sakazaki’s character will cease to exist. And those theories about contract negotiations behind the scenes? Without evidence, they remain speculation. We already have DoDon for imaginary backstories.

04 / THE AUDITIONS

The three candidates for Suica’s new mascot

Here they are. Unveiled on 8 September 2026, they are still labelled A, B and C. No invented names: even future celebrities go through a “file_final_FINAL” phase.

A

The squirrel

The pattern on its body forms a continuous line from head to tail, inspired by the railway.

Read the brief. Underlined “connections”, too.

B

The purple rabbit

Ears for listening, leaps towards the future. Purple blends the blue of calm with the red of excitement.

Looks like it knows where it’s going. Already one up on us at the station.

C

The mystery with a bag

An orange creature takes a little mole out to see the world. Its species is deliberately undefined.

It has hand luggage. The luggage has an inner life.

Concept images and descriptions: JR East’s official selection page. Jokes: we take full responsibility.

Official schedule and details ↗

In a meeting, it’s “a visual identity refresh”. In the drawer of someone back from Japan, it’s “leave my penguin alone”. That card may have no credit left, but it still holds half a holiday.

And here we are: adults with deadlines, bills and very firm opinions about a purple rabbit’s ears. All perfectly normal.

05 / THE UNINVITED CANDIDATE

What if we put DoDon
on the Suica?

Three official proposals. Then there’s him. He wasn’t invited to apply, nobody phoned, but he turned up with the card already printed. “Saved you a meeting,” he says.

“I’ve got the light to find the ticket gate. I can learn the rest.”DoDon, at an interview nobody requested

For anyone who hasn’t met him: DoDon is Kanjidon’s deep-sea fish. Eyes that say “I’ve already decided”, a built-in light and confidence that won’t fit in hand luggage.

His plan to conquer Japan is ready: first Suica. Then keyrings. Then a huge plush toy in every station. By phase four, your aunt returns from Tokyo with a DoDon on her bag and nobody remembers who authorised any of this.

The only problem is that instead of telling you your balance, he might ask you to read 駅, “station”. Excellent revision. Terrible timing if your train leaves in thirty seconds.

JR East, we’ve made our pitch. DoDon has already picked the desk by the window.
